visitor_ranger.text: Welcome to the Cliffs of Moher. In Irish they are Aillte an Mhothair, 'cliffs of the ruined fort'.
They run for about eight kilometres, and the highest point is around 214 metres above the Atlantic.
This centre is built into the hillside so it does not spoil the view. You can tell, because you did not see it coming.

then.text: That was your cuppa. The next one is in the cafe, and it costs money.

else.text: Puffins nest on the cliffs in summer. Plungebeaks dive from them, and are much less polite about it. Here, have a cuppa.

visitor_botanist.text: The Burren rock is split into blocks called clints, and plants grow in the cracks between them, called grikes.
Gentlets and burrenbloom love it. Arctic and Mediterranean flowers grow side by side, which is absurd and lovely.
